extracted.intended_audience: literate early-18th-century English public (churchgoers, coffee-house habitués, and general readers interested in conduct and elocution)
extracted.subtask_description: Periodical-essay guidance on the proper delivery of public prayer (Common Prayer) and on everyday public manners (behaviour in coffee-houses, dress, courtship, and the perils of pleasure). Offers prescriptive standards for elocution, deportment, and social conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, emphatic, and fervent reading of the Common Prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service should be read 'so distinctly, so emphatically, and so fervently' that the congregation is attentive and devout rather than distracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the reader at St. James's Garlick-Hill read 'so distinctly... that it was next to an Impossibility to be unattentive.' Affective delivery leads worshippers to feel the prayers rather than run them over 'as a matter of Form.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Due emphasis, proper accent, and apposite rising/variation of voice for prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: Prayers delivered with 'a due Emphasis, and apposite Rising and Variation of Voice, the Sentence concluded with a gentle Cadence' and 'such an Accent and Turn of Speech as is peculiar to Prayer' are most effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: place emphasis appropriately, vary tone according to sentence nature, and conclude sentences with a gentle cadence. This distinguishes prayer from ordinary reading or gazettes and makes the words affecting and humble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach English reading habits early and attend to accent/manner in schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect of English reading in school (when Latin is prized) causes bad habits: 'the Reading of which is wholly neglected... without any due Observations made to them of the proper Accent and Manner of Reading.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical remedy: instruct boys in English elocution as well as Latin; correct accent and manner early so bad habits aren't acquired and hard to remove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exemplary skilled readers as models at clergy assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes 'some Person of great Ability that way as a Pattern' to read prayers at Sion-College and other conventions so others may learn by example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational: have a celebrated reader perform at annual assemblies so clergy and readers can observe clarity, loudness, strength, posture, and fervency of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decent behaviour and erect posture while reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should avoid 'a rakish negligent Air by folding their Arms, and lolling on their Book' and instead present 'a decent Behaviour, and comely Erection of Body.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: slouched or affected postures undermine the seriousness of service; posture should reflect respect and assist audible, clear delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read deliberately and avoid excessive speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who 'Read so fast as if impatient of their Work, may learn to speak deliberately.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: moderate pace improves comprehension and devotion; train hurried readers to slow down and breathe properly between phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain evenness of voice; avoid 'Pindarick Readers' and erratic tones
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid being a 'Pindarick Reader' who is 'confined to no set measure'—alternating between over-deliberation and rapid celerity, or wildly changing tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for evenness of voice and delivery so that consecutive parts of a sentence maintain suitable, consistent treatment rather than jarring contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not domesticate or 'jazz' the language of prayer; preserve printed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should not adopt a 'Gentleman-like Familiarity of Tone, and mend the Language as they go on, crying instead of Pardoneth and Absolveth, Pardons and Absolves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the text's diction and style; avoid modernizing or altering verbs and phrases while reading public prayer, as familiarity cheapens solemnity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish elevation and emphasis from 'Cant' (avoid whining/excessive exclamation)
rubrics_metrics.description: While 'Cant' denotes 'sudden Exclamations, Whinings, unusual Tones', a proper elevation of voice, due emphasis and accent should not be mistaken for cant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should avoid whining or theatrical exclamations associated with cant, but may (and should) use skillful elevation and emphasis appropriate to prayer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Dissenting preaching faults: sudden jumps and misplaced emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissenting readers 'elevat[e] their Voices... with sudden jumps from the lower to the higher part' producing 'Bawling and Muttering', and sometimes placing emphasis on insignificant particles like 'if' or 'and'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use abrupt pitch jumps or misplace emphasis; emphasize meaningful words and phrases, not unimportant particles, to preserve sense and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that reading prayer differs from reading secular texts
rubrics_metrics.description: There is 'certainly a very great Difference between the Reading a Prayer and a Gazette'—prayer demands particular tone, cadence and reverence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train readers to adapt delivery to genre: prayers require humility and devotional tone, not the familiar or brisk manner of secular reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disruptive behaviours in public spaces (coffee-houses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public disruptors—singing voluntaries, dancing in the coffee-house, loud coughing and spitting before performing—offend company and are social transgressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern examples: a man who sang, danced, and practiced minuet-steps in a coffee-house. Sanctions suggested humorously: declare him an Outlaw, deny social comforts. Maintain decorum in shared spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be pert, talkative, or cheaply garrulous in mixed company
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Pert, the Talkative' who 'have no Sense of the Observations of others' are socially offensive and often seem not native to England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice self-restraint in company; avoid dominating conversations or showing disregard for others' sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid loud-speaking or shouting in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Loud Speakers 'treat Mankind as if we were all deaf'—they declare rather than express themselves, often out of vanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an appropriate vocal level; shouting is displeasing and imposes on others. Close the ears to neither voice nor sight by respect for decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not trade in half-accounts or secretive whispering to seem important
rubrics_metrics.description: Whisperers 'deal only in half Accounts' and employ a pattern of whispered/then-aloud speech to manufacture importance, often with nothing substantive to say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using whispering as a performance of secrecy; be candid and substantive. Whisper-based conversation that ends with 'Do not you think so?' undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: On choosing a spouse: prefer intrinsic qualities over fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding between two suitors, abstract them 'from their Circumstances' and prefer the man you would choose for his personal perfections rather than for his estate; 'employ Fortune upon Certainties, but do not sacrifice Certainties to Fortune.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether a suitor's behaviour is rooted in circumstance: would the humble poor man be as humble when rich, or the rich man as humble when poor? Choose the one whose virtues are intrinsic and transferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider whether a suitor will value you for yourself and bear with you in private
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask 'which of your Lovers will like you best undressed, which will bear with you most when out of Humour?'—choose the man who values you for yourself and will tolerate your faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess private behaviour and constancy, not just public display. Prefer the lover whose affections would remain absent fortune or show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a man whose desirable qualities are not transferable
rubrics_metrics.description: Take 'him in whom what you like is not transferable to another'—personal perfections cannot be bought by fortune in another man, whereas fortune is transferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical rule of thumb: a man chosen for intrinsic perfections is likelier to acquire external advantages than a man chosen for external advantages is to acquire intrinsic perfections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain neatness of dress; avoid affectation of slovenliness as wit
rubrics_metrics.description: The custom of 'commencing a Sloven' as the first step to being a wit debases the character; an awkward or pitiful dress prejudices hearers against what is said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for the medium between a fop and a sloven. Antipatterns: intentionally ragged dress to signal wit. Practical advice (Osbourn cited): appear rather above than below your fortune; a decent suit procures respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress in accordance with rank; do not appear beneath your quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearing 'in a Dress so much beneath his Quality and Estate' invites insult and contempt; the old gentleman in thread-bare apparel was affronted when served with stale tea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid masquerading beneath your station; dress suitably to avoid ridicule and ensure respectful treatment by service personnel and peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make pleasure the chief pursuit of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Man of Wit and Pleasure' who makes pleasure his chief pursuit becomes negligent as friend, father, and husband, leaves 'Mortgages Diseases, and Settlements' to descendants, and suffers irresolution, procrastination and moral decay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: excessive devotion to pleasure palls sensation, undermines reason, produces shameful old age, and empties life of lasting satisfaction. Cultivate moderation, industry, and virtue instead.
